title: Controv. VI: Whether there is an absolute a-priori decree of reprobation and preterition
pass_a_gloss: Whether a decree of reprobation is given — that is, of passing certain ones by with respect to grace and glory — and of divine predamnation, absolute beforehand, or independent of a cause outside God and outside His good pleasure. By that decree, God (who by freest right was able to save all and to pass by none, and to display only mercy's glory, with power sufficient in God and in Christ's satisfaction as ransom) in His eternal counsel — the counsel in which He settled what would be done or permitted outside Himself (Proverbs 16:4; Lamentations 3:37; Matthew 25:34; Acts 2:23; 15:18), and that counsel likewise immutable (Romans 9:11; 2 Timothy 2:19; Hebrews 6:17) — by an act of freest good pleasure according to the good pleasure of the will (Matthew 20:15; Romans 9:15, 20, 21, and so on), willed to leave certain people (Romans 9:13, 15, 17) and, comparatively, many (Matthew 7:13; 20:16), set in equal condition with the rest (Romans 5:12; 9:11, 21; Ephesians 2:3), in sin and misery: that is, not to choose them, not to show mercy toward salvation (Matthew 7:13; 24:40; John 13:18; Romans 8:29; 9:13, 15, and so on). From this He denies them grace — not every grace, so that they should not have a pretext (John 15:22; Romans 1:20) (invitation, for instance; urging toward duty; kindness; patience; preaching of the Word — Matthew 23:37; Romans 2:4, and so on) — yet He does deny saving grace, namely that of reconciliation through Christ (John 10:15, 26; 17:9), and likewise of effectual calling, faith, and justification (Matthew 11:26; 13:11; Romans 8:28, 29; Ephesians 2:8, and so on). Next: whether God by that same decree, as by the act of a most severe Judge (Romans 1:18, 32; 9:22), has sentenced those same people — bad and miserable by their own fault, by original misery (Romans 5:12; Ephesians 2:3) and by misery gained through actual voluntary sins against Law (Romans 2:12) or Gospel (Mark 16:16; John 3:18; 12:40), and at last unrepentant and, in various ways, despisers of God (Romans 2:4; 11:7; Matthew 10:15, and so on), each convicted by his own judgment and aware in himself of willing rebellion (Matthew 27:4; Luke 16:24, 28; Romans 2:15) — to everlasting death, to be condemned for their own sins (Proverbs 16:4; Hosea 13:9; Matthew 25:41, 42; Jude 4, and so on). Everything is for showing His freedom, power, wrath, and justice that avenges sinners (Proverbs 16:4; Matthew 20:15; Romans 9:17, 18, 20, 22, and so on).
pass_b_english: VI. Is there a decree of reprobation — or of passing certain people by as to grace and glory — and of divine predamnation, absolute from the first, independent of any cause outside God and His good pleasure?

In that decree God (who by most free right could have saved everyone, passed no one by, and shown only the glory of mercy, power being enough in God and in Christ's satisfaction as ransom) decided, in His eternal counsel about all that would be done or permitted outside Himself (Proverbs 16:4; Lamentations 3:37; Matthew 25:34; Acts 2:23; 15:18) — and that counsel is immutable (Romans 9:11; 2 Timothy 2:19; Hebrews 6:17) — by an act of most free good pleasure according to the good pleasure of His will (Matthew 20:15; Romans 9:15, 20–21, and the like), to leave certain people (Romans 9:13, 15, 17), and comparatively many (Matthew 7:13; 20:16), who stood level with the rest (Romans 5:12; 9:11, 21; Ephesians 2:3), in sin and misery: not electing them, not pitying them for salvation (Matthew 7:13; 24:40; John 13:18; Romans 8:29; 9:13, 15, and the like).

So He withholds grace from them — not every grace, lest they have a pretext (John 15:22; Romans 1:20) (invitation, urging to duty, kindness, forbearance, preaching of the Word — Matthew 23:37; Romans 2:4, and the like) — yet He does withhold saving grace, the grace of reconciliation through Christ (John 10:15, 26; 17:9), and with it effectual calling, faith, and justification (Matthew 11:26; 13:11; Romans 8:28–29; Ephesians 2:8, and the like).

And by the same decree, acting as a most severe Judge (Romans 1:18, 32; 9:22), has He adjudged those same people — evil and miserable by their own fault, under original misery (Romans 5:12; Ephesians 2:3) and misery gained by actual, voluntary sins against the Law (Romans 2:12) or the Gospel (Mark 16:16; John 3:18; 12:40), finally impenitent and in many ways despisers of God (Romans 2:4; 11:7; Matthew 10:15, and the like), each convicted by his own judgment and conscious of willing rebellion (Matthew 27:4; Luke 16:24, 28; Romans 2:15) — to eternal death, condemned for their own sins (Proverbs 16:4; Hosea 13:9; Matthew 25:41–42; Jude 4, and the like)?
All of it displays His liberty, power, wrath, and justice that avenges sins (Proverbs 16:4; Matthew 20:15; Romans 9:17–18, 20, 22, and the like).
source_text: VI. An detur Decretum Reprobationis, seu praeteritionis quorundam quoad gratiam & gloriam, ac praedamnationis divinae, absolutum a priori, seu independens a causâ extra Deum, ejusque beneplacitum: Quô scilicet Deus, (qui omnes, pro liberrimo jure, servare potuit, ac neminem praeterire, illustrareque solam misericordiae gloriam, sufficiente in Deo potentia, & in Christi satisfactione λύτρῳ) in consilio suo aeterno, quô de rebus omnibus extra sese faciendis aut permittendis statuit, Prov. XVI. 4. Lam. III. 37. Matth. XXV. 34. Act. II. 23. XV. 18. eodemque immutabili Rom. IX. 11. 2. Tim. II. 19. Hebr. VI. 17. actu liberrimi beneplaciti κατ' εὐδοκίαν τοῦ θελήματος, Matth. XX. 15. Rom. IX. 15. 20. 21. &c. certos homines Rom. IX. 13. 15. 17. & comparatè multos, Matth. VII. 13. XX. 16. in equali cum reliquis conditione positos, Rom. V. 12. IX. 11. 21. Eph. II. 3. voluit relinquere in peccato & miseria, seu non eligere, non misereri ad salutem, Matth. VII. 13. XXIV. 40. Joh. XIII. 18. Rom. VIII. 29. IX. 13. 15. &c. Hinc negare illis gratiam, non quidem omnem, praetextum ne haberent, Joh. XV. 22. Rom. I. 20. (puta invitationis, sollicitationis ad officium, beneficentiae, tolerantiae, praedicationis Verbi Matth. XXIII. 37. Rom. II. 4. &c.) sed tamen negare gratiam salutarem, seu reconciliationis illam per Christum, Joh. X. 15. 26. XVII. 9. seu etiam vocationis efficacis, fidei, justificationis, Matth. XI. 26. XIII. 11. Rom. VIII. 28. 29. Eph. II. 8. &c.? Deinde etiam, Deus eodem Decreto, ut actu severissimi Judicis, Rom. I. 18. 32. IX. 22. eosdem homines suo vitio malos & miseros, miseria ut originali, Rom. V. 12. Eph. II. 3. sic acquisita per peccata actualia, & voluntaria, seu in Legem, Rom. II. 12. seu in Evangelium Marc. XVI. 16. Joh. III. 18. XII. 40. ac finaliter impaenitentes, Deique variis modis contemptores, Rom. II. 4. XI. 7. Matth. X. 15. &c. ac suo quemque judicio convictos, sibique conscios ultroneae rebellionis, Matth. XXVII. 4. Luc. XVI. 24. 28. Rom. II. 15. adjudicarit aeternae morti, propter peccata sua damnandos, Prov. XVI. 4. Hos. XIII. 9. Matth. XXV. 41. 42. Jud. 4. &c. Omnia ad ostensionem suae libertatis, potentiae, irae, justitiae vindicis peccatorum, Prov. XVI. 4. Matt. XX. 15. Rom. IX. 17. 18. 20. 22. &c.
